findings.title: Removing the BuildIndex lock allows concurrent duplicate builds of the same key
findings.body: The whole-function lock in BuildIndex was removed and only the final cache write is now locked. Nothing else serializes builds for the same NamespacedResource. getOrCreateIndex in search.go checks GetIndex, finds nothing, and calls build. Two concurrent Search or watch-event requests for a cold namespace can therefore both reach bleve.New(dir, mapper) for the same file-based directory. The second call fails because the path already exists, or the two builds race on the same index. Even in memory, the last writer silently wins and the other index is leaked. A per-key singleflight or per-key mutex is needed to keep the 'only lock the same key' goal without allowing duplicate builds.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without holding cacheMu
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache with no lock, while BuildIndex now writes to b.cache under cacheMu.Lock at line 138. This is a data race on the map and can cause a fatal 'concurrent map read and map write' at runtime. It is called from search.init's log line, and the new log line is in the same area. The read should take cacheMu.RLock.

findings.title: Shared err and totalBatchesIndexed are written from concurrent goroutines
findings.body: Inside the errgroup loop, each goroutine does `_, _, err = s.build(...)` and `totalBatchesIndexed++`. Both variables are declared in the enclosing init scope and are shared across goroutines running with SetLimit(s.initWorkers). Concurrent writes are a data race. The error from the outer `err` can also be overwritten or misreported. The goroutine should use a local err and a local counter, or an atomic.

findings.title: Constructor now blocks on full index build and fails startup on index errors
findings.body: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init synchronously, which runs lifecycle.Init, the full search index build for every namespace (GetResourceStats plus BuildIndex), and the watcher setup. Previously this work happened lazily on the first request. Consequences: process startup now waits for every index to build, and any index or lifecycle failure makes the constructor return an error and the whole module fail to start, instead of failing individual requests. The gRPC and HTTP servers that depend on this object may also be wired before the backend is ready. The description asks what this breaks. The answer is that the failure mode and startup ordering change for every deployment, and that should be confirmed against the module wiring.

findings.title: Init failure in constructor leaks the cancelable context and background goroutines
findings.body: When s.Init fails, NewResourceServer returns nil without calling s.cancel(). The context created at line ~229 and any watcher or broadcaster started during initWatcher are never stopped. Calling s.Stop or cancel on the failure path would avoid the leak.

findings.title: Span name has a double dot
findings.body: tracePrefix already ends with '.', and the span is named tracePrefix+".GetResourceStats", which yields 'sql.resource..GetResourceStats'. The other spans in this file use tracePrefix+"WriteEvent" with no extra dot, so this name is inconsistent and wrong.

findings.title: BuildIndex still discards the span context, so the trace fix is incomplete
findings.body: The PR says it fixes trace propagation by passing span contexts down. BuildIndex still does `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)`, so the ctx it received is not propagated to its children. The same pattern exists in sql/backend.go WriteEvent, ReadResource, ListIterator and WatchWriteEvents. The description overstates what was fixed.

findings.title: Test is now silently skipped on postgres
findings.body: A new early skip for postgres was added. The test is therefore no longer exercised in CI for postgres, and the 'TODO - fix this test' comment gives no tracking reference. This is an unrelated change that reduces coverage in a PR about index startup. It should be a separate, tracked change or be removed.
